learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected about 7 percent missed and locked it in.
observations.exploration: At cutoff 1, missed and false alarms both 15.9 percent. Raised to 1.5: missed 30.9, false alarms 6.7. Lowered to 0.5: missed 6.7, false alarms 30.9. Better test at same 0.5 gave missed 2.3 and false alarms 15.9 with old values retained for comparison. Back to old test restored original values.
observations.reveal: Corrected to about 31 percent, used both threshold trials and distinguished shifting threshold from separating distributions to lower both errors at same cutoff.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected for raised cutoff, better test and reveal. Labeled healthy and sick curves, shaded missed and false-alarm tails, vertical line and percentage chips agreed. All learner explanation readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Direction commitment is useful but exact percentage requires unstated distribution knowledge.
prediction.evidence: Average and spread given, but 31 versus 7 percent not derivable from everyday numeracy alone.

interaction.reason: Two thresholds and reversible quality toggle distinguish policy from discrimination.
interaction.evidence: Both errors decreased under better test at same cutoff.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects shaded areas to reciprocal errors and improvement.

clarity.reason: Flags and both errors are plainly defined with separate denominators.
clarity.evidence: Sick people missed versus healthy false alarms labels.

transfer.reason: General tradeoff stated without a new application or decision-cost conditions.

accessibility.evidence: Text percentages and definitions available; keyboard, screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Stricter threshold misses more sick people.

visualExplanation.reason: Shaded tails and moving line make both error types visible together.
visualExplanation.evidence: Better separation reduces both shaded areas.

playfulness.reason: Threshold and quality controls invite comparisons.

depth.reason: Separates selection rule from overlapping score distributions.

complexity.reason: Easy controls hide statistical distribution prerequisites for exact prediction.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Interpret overlapping densities, tail areas and two different conditional error rates.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One cutoff slider, two presets and reversible test-quality toggle.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Score distributions, spread and density-tail percentages.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Decimal score thresholds, bell curves and percentages.

whyCool: Moving a threshold exchanges errors, while better separation can reduce both.
caveat: Exact initial percentages assume a distribution beyond the stated averages and spread; this is no real diagnostic recommendation.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
